title: Move Zeros
statement: Implement `solve(items)`. Return a new list with the same integers, zeros moved to the end, and the relative order of non-zeros unchanged.
constraints: Zero is the only value that moves
hints: Append as many zeros as you skipped.
Do not sort. Sorting would reorder the non-zeros.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: A stable partition writes non-zeros first and fills the tail with zeros.

editorial: A stable partition writes non-zeros first and fills the tail with zeros. Two pointers do this in place. Building a new list is the same partition and is easier to test. Sorting fails because 2, 1, 0 would become 0, 1, 2.
reference_solution:
def solve(items):
    nonzero = [item for item in items if item != 0]
    zeros = [0] * (len(items) - len(nonzero))
    return nonzero + zeros
